newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea SAGE gas line to shut May 21 for three weeks.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea SAGE gas line to shut May 21 for three weeks.

text.p: The Scottish Area Gas Evacuation System (SAGE) delivering gas to St Fergus in Scotland will go into maintenance on Wednesday May 21 and reopen on June 10, a spokesman for one of the participants said on Monday.
SAGE carries natural gas from the Beryl and Brae fields to St Fergus through a 210 mile, 30 inch pipeline. Average throughput is 700 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd), and capacity is 1150 mmcfd.
The pipeline is operated by Mobil North Sea Ltd and is owned by members of the Beryl group and Brae group.

One of the participants in the Beryl group said the system would run at reduced volume for the first week of maintenance, then go into total shutdown for a week, and then run at reduced volume for the third week.
But he added that while the system is running at reduced capacity, the only customers to receive gas will be those taking it under long term contracts. There will be no spot gas available.
This is not expected to affect the spot market, as potential customers have been alerted to the shutdown in advance.
